documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported a resilient operational performance for FY25, achieving a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT despite scheduled maintenance shutdowns. Management highlighted improvements in energy efficiency and the successful introduction of new value-added products like pharma-grade hexane. While GRMs were lower compared to the previous year due to international product crack trends, the company maintained a premium over Singapore benchmarks. Looking ahead, the company remains focused on operational excellence, capacity utilization, and the development of new projects like Lube Oil Based Stock (LOBS) to drive future value.

guidance.claim: The company expects to improve capacity utilization, energy intensity, and fuel efficiency in the new financial year.
guidance.quote: But yes, on the operational side, we intend to improve further on a capacity utilisation levels, on energy intensity index and fuel efficiency, we would improve on a continuous basis.

demand_outlook.claim: There is a shortfall of Motor Spirit (MS) in the southern market, estimated at approximately 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market demand for Motor Spirit is projected to grow at 4%-5%, while High Speed Diesel (HSD) is projected at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery (CBR) project is Rs 36,354 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: Maintenance CAPEX is expected to be in the range of Rs 200-250 crore annually.
capex_expansion.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

margins_costs.claim: The full-year GRM for FY25 was $4.22 per barrel, compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss for the year was reduced to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT in FY25, representing 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs 5 per equity share for the current year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity ratio as of March 31, 2025, is 0.39.
capital_allocation.quote: the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

risks_headwinds.claim: Volatility in crude prices and international product cracks pose challenges to profitability.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to conduct maintenance on one crude unit and the lubes block in FY26.
management_commitments.quote: In the current financial year 2025-26, one of the other crude units will go for maintenance along with the lubes block as such.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
